text:
jamie: Quick handoff — stitchdown for my shift. Observed a ~5min regen spike in eu-west1 around 2026-03-18T23:14Z; embeds queue grew to ~8k requests and latency climbed. Initial signals point at kvproxy throttling after the nightly backup.
deploy-bot: alert: regen-surge-eu-west1 firing x3 — threshold breach (avg latency > 350ms)

mira: I saw the same. Checked kvproxy metrics, CPU steady but connection queue length jumped. Tried a soft restart on the sidecar, no change.

jamie: I kicked a controlled restart of kvproxy on one pod to test. No immediate regression, but backlog still draining slow.

mira: Rolled restart across eu-west1-primary daemonset; commands I ran:
```
kubectl -n infra rollout restart ds/kvproxy-eu-west1
kubectl -n infra logs -f pod/kvproxy-abc --since=1h | grep -i throttle
```
Cache hit rate dipped to 52% during spike, back to ~78% after restarts.

ops-bot: nightly-backup: completed for eu-west1 at 2026-03-18T23:02Z — duration 18m. No storage errors reported.

sophia: taking bridge. I'll monitor queue length, tail app logs, and keep an eye on SLOs. If queue >10k or error rate >1.5%, I'll scale a dedicated kvproxy replica and open a rollback plan.

mira: ping @sophia on PR 1724 — backport for kvproxy connection pooling fix. That should reduce transient spikes once merged and rolled.

sophia: got it. I'll prioritize the backport review after confirming stability. Can someone drop the observability query I should watch?

jamie: watch these dashboards: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/kvproxy-eu-west1 and the quick query:
```
sum(rate(kvproxy_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le)
sum(kvproxy_queue_length) by (region)
```
Also watch embed-ingest queue: queue_length > 5000 is bad.

mira: FYI I patched a temporary rate limiter exception for a big customer flow to help drain the queue. That reduced pressure but we should revert once stable.

sophia: noted — I'll coordinate revert if we hit stable window. No blockers from my side to take over.

jamie: created INC-4728 with notes and logs (short summary + cmd history). Left a pointer to the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvproxy — basic mitigation steps + rollback checklist.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: kvproxy-backport/1724 status: pending -> queued.

mira: one follow-up — I saw two pods in CrashLoopBackOff earlier; logs showed OOMKilled on sidecar process, increased heap usage correlating with the spike. Suggest we add an OOM guard for sidecar in the next patch.

sophia: adding that to postmortem notes and the PR checklist. I'll also run a memory profile on the failing pods in the next 30m.

jamie: handoff to @sophia — bridge is yours. Current state: queue draining, kvproxy restarts done, cache hit recovered to ~78%, PR 1724 queued, temporary rate-limit exception in place, one-off CrashLoop observed but not currently active. No customer-facing impact reported yet.

sophia: taking over. I'll post a 30m update or sooner if things regress. No outstanding blockers at handoff. :thumbsup:

jamie: thanks — leaving the shift. If you need me, I'm reachable for 20m then offline. Signed off.
